u16d1-emuB: The language of capacity is dangerous to me because I do not know how to use it in a way that doesn't end up disincluding disabled people, poor people, less articulate people, people who don't have a therapeutic vocabulary, and people who are inconvenient in the moment. It does seem to require that people be clear about what criteria they are using, that the process be open to review by someone outside of it, that it be revisitable, and that this be something people are not allowed to use as a veto against people trying to join a group.
u16d2-emuA: I'm not sure how to use this language in a way that doesn't exclude disabled people and also a bunch of other people who might be poor, or not well spoken, or not well versed in therapy-speak, or even just plain old inconvenient. u16d2-emuB: I don't at present see how to make the language of capacity not exclude people with various disabilities, or who are poor, or who are not well-versed in therapy-speak, or who are just plain inconvenient. And the ability to say no to someone applying to become a member based on lack of capacity concerns me greatly.
